title: Match tuning
description: Gameplay tuning owned by the Match domain (Match Flow Bible, Battleground Bible). VeyraMatch binds it to FVeyraMatchTuning.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this file's format. A build reads exactly one version. Version 3 adds bots; version 4 replaces the fixed respawn delay with a curve and adds fountain recovery; version 5 adds Recall; version 6 moves how bots play to Bots.json (ADR-013 §5); version 7 adds absence, activity, autopilot and votes (ADR-019).

teams.description: The two sides of a match.

maxTeamSize.description: Most participants on one side; a match is 5v5 (Battleground Bible, overview).

phases.description: The in-match stages before play (Match Flow Bible §1).

loadingTimeoutSeconds.description: How long loading waits for every required participant before the match proceeds without them (Match Flow Bible §1, stage 2; prototype 90 s).

preparationSeconds.description: Length of fountain preparation before the match clock starts (Match Flow Bible §1, stage 3).

respawn.description: When a dead Vanguard returns at its fountain (Combat Bible §18): a curve over the Vanguard's level and the elapsed match time (Economy & Progression Bible §14; ADR-011 §11). The curve's values are provisional (Battleground Bible §16).

secondsByLevel.description: Seconds from a death to the respawn at each level, from Level 1; a level past the last item uses the last. 0 respawns at once.

elapsed.description: How the timer lengthens as the match goes on.

startSeconds.description: The match clock, in seconds, from which the timer starts to lengthen.

fractionPerMinute.description: What each minute past startSeconds adds, as a fraction of the level's timer.

maxFraction.description: The most the elapsed time adds, as a fraction.

fountain.description: How quickly a living Vanguard recovers at its own fountain (Battleground Bible §12; ADR-011 §11).

radius.description: How near its side's start, in units, a Vanguard must stand.

healthFractionPerSecond.description: Max Health restored each second, as a fraction.

resourceFractionPerSecond.description: Max resource restored each second, as a fraction.

recall.description: Recall: a channel that brings a living Vanguard home to its fountain (Economy & Progression Bible §10; ADR-012 §8). A new order, hostile damage and death interrupt it.

channelSeconds.description: Seconds the channel lasts, on match time.

lifecycle.description: How a match server ends its match on its own (ADR-007 §8).

abandonAfterSeconds.description: Real seconds with no rostered participant connected before the match ends as abandoned. It counts through pauses, since it is a server lifecycle clock, not a gameplay timer. Provisional: canon rules only individual disconnects (Match Flow Bible §4-5).

absence.description: Absence from a live match (Match Flow Bible §4–§6; ADR-019 §3): when a connected player counts as AFK, when absence becomes a personal loss, and how much absence a win may forgive. Every clock runs on the match clock, so a pause stops it.

afkAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of match time without meaningful activity before a connected player is warned, counted as absent, and walked to safety.

afkPenaltyAfterSeconds.description: Seconds after that warning, still inactive, before the player's personal loss is triggered.

disconnectPenaltyAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of continuous disconnection before the player's personal loss is triggered.

maxForgivenAbsentFraction.description: The largest share of the active match duration a player may have been absent, in total, for a win to forgive their personal loss.

activity.description: What counts as meaningful activity (Match Flow Bible §5.1; ADR-019 §3): accepted move, attack, cast, rank-up and Recall orders; never shopping or chat.

minimumMoveDistance.description: How far, in units, a move order's destination must be from the last one counted for the move to count, so repeated input in place does not.

autopilot.description: Where an absent Vanguard is walked (Match Flow Bible §4; ADR-019 §2): behind the nearest standing allied tower, then home to its fountain. It only moves.

fountainAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of match time after it starts before the autopilot turns for the fountain.

behindTowerDistance.description: How far behind the tower, in units along its lane toward home, the autopilot stops.

votes.description: Remake, surrender and pause votes (Match Flow Bible §7–§10; ADR-019 §4). Windows, cooldowns and the intermission are real seconds; the start conditions are match time.

remake.description: Either team may start one before startBeforeSeconds; only it votes; a disconnected teammate votes YES.

startBeforeSeconds.description: Match seconds after which no remake vote may start; one already started may finish.

yesVotes.description: YES votes that pass it: a majority of teams.maxTeamSize.

cooldownSeconds.description: Seconds after a failed vote before the same team may start another.

surrender.description: Either team may start one from startAfterSeconds; only it votes; a disconnected teammate abstains.

startAfterSeconds.description: Match seconds before which no surrender vote may start.

yesVotes.description: YES votes that pass it: a majority of teams.maxTeamSize.

cooldownSeconds.description: Seconds after a failed vote before the same team may start another.

pause.description: Anyone may start one while the match is live; it passes only when every player votes YES, and an AFK or disconnected player votes YES. The intermission it opens resumes by itself, or early on another unanimous vote.

cooldownSeconds.description: Seconds after a failed pause vote before another may start.

intermissionSeconds.description: Real seconds a passed pause lasts before play resumes by itself.

orders.description: How the server accepts a player's move orders (ADR-006 §7: server-only movement). Provisional values.

maxPerSecond.description: Sustained orders a player may send per second; the server refuses the rest.

destinationProjectionExtent.description: How far, in units along each axis, a clicked destination may lie from walkable ground and still be accepted.

arrivalTolerance.description: How close, in units, a Vanguard must come to its destination to have arrived.

developerMatch.description: Developer matches until champion select (ADR-008 §8): the Vanguard each participant plays, by join order, and a head start on ranks. Hosted matches use the same order.

vanguards.description: The Vanguard each participant plays, in join order; the last one plays for every later joiner. Each is a content ID that Vanguards.json defines. A development build's -VeyraVanguard= option overrides it for one client.

startingRank.description: The slot a developer match spends each participant's level-1 skill point on, so its Vanguard can cast at once; None leaves the choice to the player.
